questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It was crucial for me that it was a country I would feel comfortable in. I also wanted to study at a university that I had heard good thing about beforehand.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: At Luiss, a welcome meeting was held for all exchange students before the classes began. All the information that I needed to know was touched upon at that meeting.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Look at the abovementioned.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found my housing through af Facebook-page. However, I know that a lot of exchange students had troubles finding any, so maybe start looking for housing early on in the proces

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It was nice to live off campus and to live much nearer the city. However, the campus can be a bit far away and it therefore takes a lot of time to get to the campus, if you choose to live near the city instead.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: In mid-June, a list of courses offered during the semester was sent out. In this mail there were also instructions on how to proceed.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Luiss had issued some instructions that you just had to follow. Also the Student Mobility at Luiss was really helpful, when I had any questions.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the courses I wanted. You also had the opportunity to try out the courses for a while and then change your choices if you needed to.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you have any questions, you can always contact Student Mobility at Luiss.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It was very different how the level was in the different courses. In some courses there were only exchange students, while in others there was a majority of Italian students. In addition, the amount of preparation in the different courses varied greatly.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It depended a lot on which course you had. In some courses it was a requirement to be active, as your grade is partly based on this. There were also some courses where there was a lot of group work. In other courses, there was just one professor talking the whole way through.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Data Protection Law, EU Law before Court: Rights and Procedures, Managing and Financing the Energy Transition, European Administrative Law and International Arbitration

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I would particularly recommend the Data Protection Law and International Arbitration courses. 

The reason I would recommend Data Protection Law is that it is one of the courses I have learned the most in. In addition, I also imagine that I will benefit from it in the future. The downside of it is that there are three mid-term tests along the way, each of which counts 25% of the total grade. 

In addition, I would recommend international arbitration, as it was the course I found the most interesting

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: I was very lucky to find a cheap apartment, so the cost was much lower than I expected. In addition, living in general in Rome was also cheaper than I expected - especially eating out.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were a lot of activities. You could sign up for different sports teams. In addition, ESN planned a lot of social things for exchange students.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I would recommend others to go and visit some other cities in Italy. It gives you a very good insight on the difference between the north and the south, and you'll get to learn Italys culture much better.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I think it was easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I think the most challenging part was that not all italians speak English, so it was a bit hard to communicate sometimes

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The italians are very open to foreigners

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Just enjoy it and relax. Even though the exam period can seem a bit stresfull, everything is going to work out just fine.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The new friendships that I made

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Being away from home for that long time

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
